description: Painted cloud atlas for globally placed map atmosphere.
prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept. Asset type: transparent PNG sprite atlas of small atmospheric clouds for an existing painted fantasy board-game map.
Create exactly TWELVE different isolated cloud shapes in exactly FOUR equal columns and THREE equal rows, row-major, canvas1536x1152. One cloud centered in each cell. Each cloud is a gently horizontal compact form, at most65% cell width and45% cell height, generous transparent space between all12.
Style: a single cohesive European storybook gouache painting style, viewed from gently above, soft upper-left lighting. Quiet warm ivory/pearl white upper lobes, very light desaturated blue-grey undersides. Soft feathered semitransparent edges, light drybrush strokes, enough hand-painted organic texture to match miniature fantasy map scenery. These will overlay terrain at only50–100pixels wide so simple distinct silhouettes matter. All clouds from the same world and palette. Airy and lightweight, never dark storm banks, no heavy grey shadows, no thick outlines, no shiny3D/toy look, no emoji/icon cartoons, no faces or rainbow colors.
Exact distinct shapes row-major:
1. small fluffy three-lobed cumulus with a softly flattened base
2. long low wispy cloud ribbon with two soft breaks
3. two linked rounded puffs with a faint trailing wisp to the right
4. thin wind-stretched torn cloud veil
5. squat wide soft cumulus with an uneven gently scalloped top
6. small curled wind tuft, graceful slight hook
7. two softly overlapping thin cloud banks
8. ragged airy cloud fragment with a soft tapered end
9. three small loose puffs forming one horizontal group
10. very light curved feathery cirrus streak
11. soft crescent-shaped mountain mist tuft
12. compact rounded cluster with a long fine tail to the left.
Genuine transparent alpha background with semi-transparent fringes. NO sky backdrop, haze rectangle, opaque ground, checkerboard pattern, drop shadows, labels, text, grid lines, birds or mountains. Strict4x3 grid. Actual alpha0 in every gap between clouds.
